title: A full subcategory closed under kernels, cokernels and sums is abelian with exact inclusion
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] and $\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal A$ a full subcategory such that (i) some zero object of $\mathcal A$ lies in $\mathcal C$; (ii) for every morphism $f$ between objects of $\mathcal C$, every object of $\mathcal A$ that is a kernel of $f$ in $\mathcal A$, and every object of $\mathcal A$ that is a cokernel of $f$ in $\mathcal A$, lies in $\mathcal C$; (iii) for objects $A,B$ of $\mathcal C$ every product $A\times B=A\oplus B$ in $\mathcal A$ lies in $\mathcal C$. Then $\mathcal C$, with the addition of morphisms of $\mathcal A$, is an abelian category; a kernel (resp. cokernel) in $\mathcal A$ of a morphism of $\mathcal C$ is a kernel (resp. cokernel) of it in $\mathcal C$; and a sequence $0\to A\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{g}C\to0$ of objects and morphisms of $\mathcal C$ is a short exact sequence of $\mathcal C$ if and only if it is a short exact sequence of $\mathcal A$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence].
